articles.title: Why are bond yields rising and how does it affect me?
articles.summary: Some government borrowing costs have hit their highest level for 28 years - what does it mean for you?
articles.body:
UK government borrowing costs have been rising, with some now at their highest level since 1998 as investors around the world worry about inflation.

Why is this happening and how does it affect you?

A bond is a bit like an IOU that can be traded in the financial markets.

Governments generally spend more than they raise in tax so they borrow money to fill the gap, usually by selling bonds to investors.

As well as eventually paying back the value of the bond, governments pay interest at regular intervals so investors receive a stream of future payments.

UK government bonds - known as "gilts" - are normally considered very safe, with little risk the money will not be repaid. They are mainly bought by financial institutions, such as pension funds.

Interest rates - known as the yield - on government bonds have been going up, with the yield on a 10-year bond at its highest level since 2008, while the yield on a 30-year bond is at its highest since 1998, meaning it costs the government more to borrow over the long term.

This comes at a sensitive time for new PM Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey as they prepare for their first budget on 28 October.

The government's ability to play with the public finances is limited by the so-called fiscal rules it has set for itself.

So, if it needs more money to pay back higher borrowing costs, it has less to spend on other things (under its self-imposed rules).

The possibility now looms of less support for households struggling with the cost of living, or of tax rises to pay for any support.

Importantly, these are choices – not certainties – so the chancellor might free up some money by spending less elsewhere.

Some may be wondering about the impact of higher gilt yields on the mortgage market, particularly after what followed Liz Truss's mini-Budget in September 2022.

Analysts believe that mortgage rates could go up on new fixed deals, as funding costs for lenders rise. But this is very different to 2022, when they shot up over a couple of days.

That speedy rise led to lenders quickly pulling deals while they tried to work out what interest rate to charge.

However, the market could be more favourable to anyone currently buying an annuity - a product from an insurance company that gives a retirement income for the rest of their life, bought only once.

Yields are rising not just in the UK. Borrowing costs have also been going up in the US, Japan and Europe

Investors worry that events in the Middle East mean high oil prices, and rising inflation in general, will persist.

If inflation is high, then the purchasing power of fixed payments is diluted. So, investors demand a higher yield as compensation, and sell off their bonds.

Investors are also increasingly concerned about high levels of government borrowing, while there has been greater demand for loans from big tech companies hoping to fund investment in AI - driving up competition and increasing the interest rate lenders demand.

articles.title: People just brazenly ask: 'Have you got any cheap tobacco?'
articles.summary: Mohammed Rajak says shops selling illicit tobacco and vapes are the biggest threat to his business.
articles.body:
Mohammed Rajak has run his family grocery store in Glasgow's East End for 35 years.

He's seen his business change over that time, but he says the biggest threat to his livelihood right now are shops selling illicit tobacco and vapes.

He says his own shop does not sell such products but there are stores very close by that do.

"Sometimes they even come in and say: 'Oh, we've come to the wrong shop'.

"It used to be they would lower their voices. Now it's just brazen: 'Have you got any cheap tobacco?'."

Rajak says he watches as people he has refused to serve walk to the shop he suspects of selling illicit products.

He says they'll sell to anyone, including children, because they're operating without risk.

"You wouldn't you go into a shop and buy out-of-date medicine because it's going to be harmful for you, so I don't know why you'd so something similar with illicit tobacco and vapes," he says.

Busting the tobacco bandits with Boo the dog

Police target barbers and vape shops in organised crime raids

Illegal mini-marts to shut for up to 12 months under law change prompted by BBC

Trading Standards has described the proliferation of shops selling illicit tobacco as an "explosion" across Scotland's high streets.

The products could have been legally produced for another country but are often made in small unregulated factories that do not comply with any safety rules.

It's these products that are the biggest worry.

Tests have shown they can contain rat droppings and woodchips among other harmful substances.

Buying cheap cigarettes isn't just about not paying tax duty.

Trading Standards say it also directly supports organised crime.

Inverness isn't the sort of place where you'd expect organised crime, but the increase in illicit tobacco there demonstrates the long arms of the gangs involved.

Trading Standards and HMRC recently raided a shop there suspected of selling illicit tobacco.

It was the 11th time Trading Standards had been at the premises since 2024 and the ninth time they'd found or been sold illicit tobacco.

The officer in charge on the day, who wants to remain anonymous, said: "We're doing as much as we can, but it's very disappointing.

"We could go in every day of the week, and we'd probably find something."

Having found the illicit products, officers bag them up and take them away for further investigation.

They then submit a referral to HMRC who make a further decision on a monetary penalty for the business owner.

These are separate powers from the ones Trading Standards have.

Right now, Trading Standards in Scotland can only issue Fixed Penalty Notices to individuals caught selling tobacco and vapes to underage buyers.

They don't have the regulatory powers of their counterparts in England and Wales to apply to close the businesses.

BBC Scotland News wanted to know how often their existing powers were being used.

Freedom of Information requests were submitted to all of Scotland's councils to ask how many fixed penalty notices had been issued by Trading Standards over the past 10 years.

These could be for underage sales or other breaches like incorrect tobacco display or not asking for age verification.

The responses suggest enforcement activity varies across the country.

They show that North Lanarkshire issued 243 fixed penalty notices, whereas Angus, Comhairle nan Eilean Siar (Western Isles), East Renfrewshire, North Ayrshire, Orkney, Scottish Borders and Shetland issued fewer than 10 each.

East Lothian only held information for the past five years but had not conducted any raids or test purchases.

Over the past 10 years, the figures also suggest underage vaping has become an increasing focus for Trading Standards officers.

They will often use what is known as test purchasing, where a minor will buy cigarettes or vapes in a shop, allowing Trading Standards to issue the fixed penalty notices.

David MacKenzie, chair of the Chartered Trading Standards Institute and head of Trading Standards at Highland Council, says stopping traders in illicit nicotine could be easier if the Scottish government gave them powers comparable to those available south of the border.

"This crime really threatens our communities," he says.

"Organised crime has long been an issue in our big cities, but now it's everywhere."

Although Trading Standards are working to capacity, they would like to do more.

"Some businesses do take the warning and change what they do," MacKenzie says.

"But some others are repeat offenders and it's very frustrating to deal with them."

Public health experts say the issue extends beyond lost tax revenues and unfair competition for legitimate businesses.

People buying illicit tobacco and vaping products may not know what ingredients they contain or whether they meet UK safety standards.

Dr Garth Reid, consultant in public health at Public Health Scotland, says: "Illicit tobacco and vape products undermine efforts to protect health.

"They are cheap, readily available and sold outside the safeguards that apply to regulated products."

The Scottish government minister for victims and community safety, Kirsten Oswald, told BBC News that high street organised crime and illicit tobacco were serious issues.

She said the government was looking at the reality of the situation to establish the best way to tackle the problem going forward.

articles.title: O que ajuda o mico-leão-dourado também pode representar um risco | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo revela que a conexão entre fragmentos florestais, essencial para a conservação da espécie, pode ampliar a mortalidade durante surtos de febre amarela.
articles.summary: Estudo revela que a conexão entre fragmentos florestais, essencial para a conservação da espécie, pode ampliar a mortalidade durante surtos de febre amarela.
articles.body:
Mico-Leão-Dourado (Leontopithecus rosalia) — Foto: henrique_bitencourt

A conexão entre fragmentos de Mata Atlântica, normalmente benéfica para a sobrevivência do mico-leão-dourado, pode ter um efeito diferente durante uma epidemia de febre amarela .

Um estudo recente publicado no Journal of Applied Ecology identificou que áreas mais conectadas apresentaram menor sobrevivência dos animais durante o surto registrado entre 2017 e 2019.

A pesquisa analisou o mico-leão-dourado ( Leontopithecus rosalia ), espécie ameaçada de extinção encontrada na Mata Atlântica do Rio de Janeiro. Segundo o estudo, aproximadamente 30% da população foi perdida durante o período da epidemia .

Os pesquisadores utilizaram dados de três décadas de monitoramento, coletados entre 1989 e 2022. Para avaliar os efeitos da febre amarela, compararam a sobrevivência dos animais entre 2014 e 2016, antes do surto, e entre 2017 e 2019, durante a circulação da doença.

A análise reuniu informações de 300 animais: 145 acompanhados no período anterior à epidemia e 155 durante o surto. Os cientistas avaliaram fatores como cobertura florestal, conectividade entre fragmentos, densidade populacional humana, distância de estradas e tamanho dos grupos.

Veja mais notícias do Terra da Gente, no g1:

Conexão que protege também pode representar risco

Antes do surto, a maior conectividade entre os fragmentos estava relacionada ao aumento da sobrevivência dos micos. Durante a epidemia, porém, essa associação se inverteu.

Segundo os pesquisadores, no estudo, “a conectividade do habitat aumentou a sobrevivência antes do surto, mas ampliou a mortalidade durante a epidemia”.

Uma das explicações discutidas no artigo é que fragmentos conectados facilitam a movimentação dos micos e trazem benefícios para a conservação da espécie. Durante uma epidemia, entretanto, essa mesma configuração também pode favorecer o deslocamento de mosquitos e ampliar as oportunidades de contato entre os animais e os vetores infectados.

Animal quase foi extinto na década de 1970. — Foto: Carlos Henrique Ferreira

O resultado não significa que os pesquisadores recomendem interromper corredores ecológicos ou isolar áreas de floresta. O estudo mostra que os efeitos da conectividade podem mudar conforme o contexto e que o risco de doenças precisa ser considerado no planejamento das ações de conservação.

Durante o surto, a menor cobertura florestal e a maior densidade populacional humana também estiveram associadas à redução da sobrevivência dos micos.

Segundo os pesquisadores, o “impacto humano, mais do que o clima, teve papel central” na distribuição do risco de mortalidade.

As variáveis climáticas analisadas não apareceram como preditores significativos.

Os autores, no entanto, reconhecem que os dados climáticos utilizados representavam médias de longo prazo e poderiam não captar variações sazonais importantes para a presença dos mosquitos.

O estudo também ressalta que nem todas as mortes puderam ser confirmadas como provocadas pela febre amarela . Como encontrar carcaças na floresta é difícil, os pesquisadores consideraram como mortos os animais que desapareceram de grupos que continuaram monitorados e não foram encontrados posteriormente em outros grupos.

Mico-leão-dourado é primata exclusivo do Brasil — Foto: Luciano Lima

A partir dos resultados, os cientistas produziram mapas das áreas com maior probabilidade de mortalidade durante o surto . O risco mais elevado apareceu principalmente em locais com baixa cobertura florestal, maior densidade humana e maior conectividade entre os fragmentos.

De acordo com o artigo, essas projeções podem ajudar a definir áreas prioritárias para a vacinação dos micos-leões-dourados . Fragmentos que funcionam como pontes entre populações podem receber atenção especial, já que a imunização nesses pontos teria potencial para reduzir a propagação do vírus pela paisagem.

Os autores alertam, porém, que o mapa deve ser combinado com outras informações, como o número de animais em cada área, a facilidade de acesso aos grupos, a disponibilidade de vacinas e o avanço de um eventual surto.

articles.title: Sou Manaus 2026: Prazo extra para retirar pulseiras termina hoje | G1
articles.standfirst: Retirada exige documento com foto, comprovante da reserva e 1 quilo de alimento não perecível.
articles.summary: Garanta sua entrada no Sou Manaus Passo a Paço 2026 levando documento, reserva e alimento não perecível aos pontos de troca autorizados pela ManausCult hoje.
articles.body:
Ferrugem, Gustavo Mioto e Natanzinho Lima são atrações do Sou Manaus 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A Prefeitura de Manaus prorrogou até esta quarta-feira (2) o prazo para retirada das pulseiras do festival "Sou Manaus Passo a Paço 2026" . A decisão atende quem fez a reserva, mas não conseguiu retirar o ingresso na data marcada.

As pulseiras dão acesso aos shows gratuitos do festival, que acontecem de 4 a 7 de setembro, no Centro Histórico de Manaus. Ana Castela, Dennis DJ, Iza, Léo Santana, Filipe Ret, Gustavo Mioto e Gloria Groove estão entre as atrações.

Para garantir a pulseira, era necessário fazer o cadastro na plataforma oficial do evento . A reserva é trocada pela pulseira mediante a doação de 1 quilo de alimento não perecível.

A ManausCult reforça que os participantes devem conferir o comprovante e ir ao ponto correto para garantir agilidade e organização no atendimento.

O diretor-presidente da ManausCult, Márcio Braz, destacou que a retirada extra acontece apenas nesta quarta-feira (2) e alertou para que o público fique atento aos locais e horários.

"Estamos criando essa oportunidade para que ninguém que tenha feito a reserva fique de fora do Sou Manaus 2026. É importante ficar atento: a retirada será feita somente nesta quarta-feira (2), nos pontos e horários divulgados", disse Márcio Braz.

articles.title: Curso de empreendedorismo feminino em Sorocaba: aulas de IA e mais | G1
articles.standfirst: Promovido pelo Instituto Mulheres que Decidem, o projeto 'Mulher Decidida Digital 3.0' reúne imersão presencial e módulos virtuais no fim de setembro.
articles.summary: O projeto Mulher Decidida Digital 3.0 abre inscrições em Sorocaba para capacitação gratuita com foco em inteligência artificial, finanças e oratória no final de setembro.
articles.body:
Sorocaba recebe curso gratuito de empreendedorismo feminino com aulas de IA, finanças e oratória — Foto: Divulgação

O Instituto Mulheres que Decidem realiza em Sorocaba (SP) a formação gratuita “Mulher Decidida Digital 3.0”, voltada para mulheres que desejam iniciar um negócio ou aprimorar empreendimentos em andamento. O programa combina dois dias de imersão presencial, nos dias 25 e 26 de setembro, e um mês de capacitação on-line.

A imersão presencial será realizada no Espaço Now Sorocaba, localizado na Avenida Roberto Simonsen, nº 450, no bairro Santa Rosália.

As atividades ocorrem das 9h às 18h na sexta-feira (25) e das 8h às 18h30 no sábado (26). A participação é gratuita, mas as vagas são limitadas, e as interessadas devem realizar o cadastro prévio por meio do formulário oficial do evento.

Criado há 25 anos, o Instituto Mulheres que Decidem já prestou atendimento a mais de 40 mil mulheres em todo o país. A formação conta com a participação de profissionais voluntárias de diferentes setores que compartilham experiências de mercado.

A grade curricular aborda áreas estratégicas para a gestão e o desenvolvimento de negócios de pequeno porte. A aplicação da inteligência artificial no cotidiano das empresas será um dos focos, com orientações práticas para a criação de conteúdo, planejamento e organização das atividades diárias.

O conteúdo também inclui orientações sobre gestão financeira, estratégias para ampliação da presença no ambiente virtual por meio do marketing digital, além de treinamentos de oratória e desenvolvimento de mentalidade empreendedora para auxiliar no posicionamento das participantes no mercado.

articles.title: Gracindo Jr., ator e diretor que participou da inauguração da TV Globo, morre no Rio aos 83 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Ele atuou em novelas e programas que fizeram história na emissora e era filho de outro ator consagrado, Paulo Gracindo.
articles.summary: Ele atuou em novelas e programas que fizeram história na emissora e era filho de outro ator consagrado, Paulo Gracindo.
articles.body:
O ator e diretor Gracindo Jr . morreu na noite desta terça-feira (1) em casa, no Rio de Janeiro . Ele tinha 83 anos, dos quais mais de 50 anos foram dedicados à arte no teatro, rádio e cinema — e participou da inauguração da Globo , em 1965.

A informação do falecimento foi confirmada por Pedro Gracindo, filho do artista. A morte foi por causas naturais.

O velório, aberto ao público , está previsto para esta quinta-feira (3), no Crematório e Cemitério da Penitência, a partir das 12h10. A cremação foi marcada para as 14h10.

Ele deixa 5 filhos , 7 netos e a esposa, Daisy Poli , com quem estava havia mais de 50 anos .

Epaminondas Xavier Gracindo nasceu no Rio de Janeiro, em 21 de maio de 1943, filho de outro ator consagrado, Paulo Gracindo (1911-1995).

Embora tenha cursado Psicologia, nunca exerceu a profissão , optando por se dedicar integralmente à arte.

Em 1959, aos 15 anos, Gracindo Jr. fez um teste para trabalhar na Rádio Nacional, onde o pai já fazia sucesso como galã de radionovelas e apresentador de programas de auditório.

O filho foi aprovado e foi ator, redator e disc-jóquei na emissora.

Em 1961, em paralelo às funções na rádio, estreou no teatro na peça “A Escada”, de Oswald de Andrade.

Gracindo Jr. em depoimento ao Memória Globo. — Foto: Foto: Frame de vídeo/Memória Globo

Em 1965, foi inaugurada a TV Globo. Em entrevista ao Memória Globo , o ator disse: “Eu entrei no início da TV Globo. Ela estreia em abril de 1965, em dezembro de 1964 eu já estava contratado ”.

Gracindo Jr. integrou o 1º elenco da emissora e participou de várias novelas dessa fase inicial, como “Rosinha do Sobrado”, “Padre Tião”, “A Rainha Louca”, “A Próxima Atração”, “Supermanoela” e “Os Ossos do Barão” — quando contracenou com Paulo Gracindo.

Pai e filho voltaram a dividir o set em “O Bem Amado”, de Dias Gomes, e em “O Casarão”, de Lauro César Muniz, quando interpretaram as versões jovem e idosa de João Maciel, protagonista da trama — o 1º grande papel de Gracindo Jr.

“O que eu mais aprendi com o meu pai foi responsabilidade no meu trabalho, estima pelo meu trabalho, saber que meu trabalho é uma coisa muito importante”, declarou.

“Meu pai trabalhou por 65 anos, e nunca me lembro dele não tendo feito sucesso, em qualquer área de comunicação. Foi um homem que passou em rádio, em circo, em televisão, em cinema, em tudo ele foi sucesso”, prosseguiu.

“A lembrança que eu tenho dele é dessa pessoa delicada, dessa pessoa amiga, solidária e que seu maior amor era o seu trabalho. Se o trabalho dele estivesse bem-feito, ele estava feliz na vida.”

Gracindo Jr. e o pai, o também ator Paulo Gracindo, durante a novela 'O Bem Amado' — Foto: TV Globo/ Cedoc

Gracindo Jr. atuou também em sucessos como “Mandala”, “O Salvador da Pátria”, “Rainha da Sucata”, “Deus nos Acuda”, “Explode Coração”, “Anjo de Mim”, “Esplendor” e “Celebridade”.

O artista também se consagrou como diretor. Ele dirigiu produções de sucesso como a novela “Marron-Glacé” e, em 1983, dirigiu o programa “Os Trapalhões”.

Gracindo Jr. também participou da criação e apresentação dos primeiros videoclipes de artistas brasileiros exibidos pelo Fantástico.

articles.title: Treinos em academias públicas de Salvador têm novo tipo de agendamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Não será mais necessário baixar o aplicativo para agendar os treinos. Nova plataforma também tem vídeos dos exercícios.
articles.summary: Não será mais necessário baixar o aplicativo para agendar os treinos. Nova plataforma também tem vídeos dos exercícios.
articles.body:
Academia pública de Salvador — Foto: Vitor Santos/ Sempre

As academias públicas de Salvador terão um novo método de agendamento, conforme informado pela Secretaria Municipal de Promoção Social, Combate à Pobreza, Esportes e Lazer (Sempre) na terça-feira (1º).

O agendamento do treino, que antes era feito no aplicativo, agora deve ser feito através do site . A alteração foi feita foi feita após os usuários reclamarem sobre a falta de memória nos celulares.

Quem já é cadastrado no portal não precisa refazer o cadastro, basta acessar e agendar as aulas. A nova plataforma ainda tem funções novas, como vídeos de profissionais com orientações sobre a forma correta de fazer cada exercício.

Atualmente, são 15 academias públicas em Salvador, nos bairros de Amaralina, Barros Reis, Boca do Rio, Bonfim, Cajazeiras, Calabar, Dique do Tororó, Imbuí, Itapuã, Largo do Tanque, Mané Dendê, Narandiba, São Caetano, São Tomé de Paripe e no canteiro central da Avenida Bonocô.

Juntas, elas têm cerca de 35 mil usuários fixos, que são aqueles que utilizam o serviço pelo menos duas vezes por semana.

As academias contam com 89 professores formados em Educação Física e cerca de 30 estagiários, além de recepcionistas.

articles.title: Cephas abre 440 vagas para cursos técnicos gratuitos em São José | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições para o Vestibulinho 2027 vão até o dia 3 de novembro e há oportunidades em 8 áreas de formação.
articles.summary: Inscrições para o Vestibulinho 2027 vão até o dia 3 de novembro e há oportunidades em 8 áreas de formação.
articles.body:
O Colégio de Educação Profissional Hélio Augusto de Souza (Cephas), em São José dos Campos , abriu 440 vagas para cursos técnicos gratuitos para o primeiro semestre de 2027. As oportunidades estão distribuídas entre 11 turmas de oito cursos.

As inscrições começaram nesta terça-feira (1º) e podem ser feitas pela internet até 3 de novembro . A taxa é de R$ 25. Candidatos que não tiverem condições financeiras podem solicitar a isenção até o dia 23 de outubro.

Cada turma oferece 40 vagas e as oportunidades são para Administração, Enfermagem, Mecânica, Cuidados de Idosos, Edificações, Eletrônica e Química.

Os cursos têm duração de até quatro semestres e são oferecidos nos períodos da manhã, tarde e noite. As vagas são destinadas a quem já concluiu o Ensino Médio ou a estudantes que estarão regularmente matriculados no segundo ou terceiro ano do ensino médio em fevereiro de 2027.

Um dos critérios para participar do processo seletivo é morar em São José dos Campos há pelo menos dois anos. A comprovação será exigida no momento da matrícula.

A prova será realizada de forma online, entre os dias 12 e 14 de novembro. O candidato poderá escolher a data no momento da inscrição.

articles.title: MP entra na Justiça e cobra vagas em creches e pré-escolas Cabo Frio | G1
articles.standfirst: A ação civil pública foi ajuizada no dia 27 de agosto pela 3ª Promotoria de Justiça de Tutela Coletiva do Núcleo Cabo Frio.
articles.summary: A ação civil pública foi ajuizada no dia 27 de agosto pela 3ª Promotoria de Justiça de Tutela Coletiva do Núcleo Cabo Frio.
articles.body:
O Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ) entrou na Justiça para que a Prefeitura de Cabo Frio , na Região dos Lagos do Rio, amplie a oferta de vagas em creches e pré-escolas da rede municipal.

Em 2025, 767 crianças estavam na demanda não atendida pela educação infantil no município.

A ação civil pública foi ajuizada no dia 27 de agosto pela 3ª Promotoria de Justiça de Tutela Coletiva do Núcleo Cabo Frio.

Segundo dados reunidos pelo Ministério Público, entre 2022 e 2025, a rede municipal criou 67 novas vagas em creches e 78 na pré-escola.

Na ação, o MPRJ pede, em caráter liminar, que as crianças que já estão cadastradas e aguardam uma vaga sejam matriculadas na rede pública em até 90 dias. Para novos pedidos de matrícula, o prazo solicitado é de até 45 dias.

Caso não haja vaga disponível na rede pública dentro desses prazos, o Ministério Público pede que o município garanta a matrícula da criança na rede particular, com os custos pagos pela Prefeitura.

O pedido inclui ainda despesas necessárias para o acesso e a permanência do aluno, como transporte, alimentação e material didático.

A medida busca garantir o atendimento da demanda por educação infantil no município. A ação civil pública é um instrumento utilizado pelo Ministério Público para pedir à Justiça medidas destinadas à proteção de direitos coletivos.

Neste caso, o processo trata do direito de acesso à educação de crianças em idade de creche e pré-escola.

A Prefeitura de Cabo Frio foi questionada sobre o número atual de vagas disponíveis na educação infantil e a quantidade de crianças que permanecem na fila de espera. O município informou que ainda não havia sido notificado sobre a ação e, até o momento da resposta, não apresentou os dados solicitados.

articles.title: Killing at Sea
articles.summary: Three families, two bombings and a hidden war: uncovering the lives behind Operation Southern Spear’s dead.
articles.body:
Since September 2025, the US military has carried out more than 60 strikes on suspected drug-trafficking boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific, killing more than 220 people.

In a military campaign called Operation Southern Spear, President Donald Trump’s administration has claimed to wage war against “narcoterrorism”. Yet the government has released little information about who was killed, the evidence against them or how targets were selected.

In Killing at Sea, Fault Lines investigates the administration’s claims about Operation Southern Spear by uncovering the stories of those targeted and the evidence used to justify lethal military force.

Through the stories of families left searching for answers, alongside witness accounts, physical evidence and interviews with legal experts, Fault Lines asks whether the strikes are lawful, whether they have disrupted the drug trade and what accountability exists for those killed.

From fishing communities in the Caribbean to Washington, DC, Killing at Sea examines a military campaign conducted largely beyond public view—and asks who is being killed in the US’s new war at sea, and why.

articles.title: Morre Juracy Palhano, político e fundador de bairro em Campina Grande | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-parlamentar teve uma trajetória marcada por atuações na política, educação, rádio e urbanização de Campina Grande.
articles.summary: O ex-deputado Juracy Palhano faleceu aos 91 anos, deixando um legado na política, educação e no desenvolvimento urbano de Campina Grande e da Paraíba.
articles.body:
Juracy Palhano, ex-deputado e fundador do bairro das Nações, em Campina Grande — Foto: Reprodução/TV Paraíba

Morreu aos 91 anos o empresário, ambientalista e político João Juracy Palhano Freire , responsável por fundar um dos primeiros loteamentos de Campina Grande , no Agreste da Paraíba, que deu origem ao bairro das Nações. A informação foi confirmada pela família nesta quarta-feira (2).

Juracy Palhano foi uma figura de destaque na história de Campina Grande, com atuação em áreas como política, educação, comunicação e urbanização. Ao longo da vida pública, participou da criação de escolas, trabalhou como locutor e contribuiu para o desenvolvimento urbano da cidade.

Uma das principais contribuições de Juracy para Campina Grande aconteceu na área de urbanização. Ele foi responsável pela criação de bairros e loteamentos arborizados, a exemplo do bairro das Nações, na Zona Norte da cidade, e do loteamento Cidade Juracy Palhano.

Natural do distrito de Lagoa de Remígio, que pertencia ao município de Areia e posteriormente passou a integrar Remígio, Juracy Palhano iniciou a carreira política em 1968, quando foi eleito vereador de Remígio. Em 1974, chegou à Assembleia Legislativa da Paraíba como deputado estadual e foi reeleito quatro anos depois.

Durante a trajetória política, disputou duas vezes a Prefeitura de Campina Grande, em 1972 e 1976, mas não foi eleito. Em 1982, tentou uma vaga na Câmara Federal e, em 1986, assumiu o mandato como suplente após o afastamento de Joacil Pereira. Posteriormente, tornou-se deputado federal titular após a morte de Ernani Sátyro. A última candidatura de Juracy Palhano ocorreu em 1990, quando disputou o Governo da Paraíba.

Antes de ingressar na política, Juracy também atuou na área da educação. Ele foi diretor do Colégio Estadual de Campina Grande, hoje conhecido como Estadual da Prata, e participou da implantação de escolas estaduais nos bairros de Bodocongó, Liberdade e José Pinheiro.

Juracy também teve passagem pelo rádio e atuou como locutor em programas transmitidos em Campina Grande.

O velório de Juracy Palhano acontece a partir das 12h desta quarta-feira (2), em uma central de velórios no bairro São José, em Campina Grande.

O sepultamento está previsto para esta quinta-feira (3), no Cemitério Municipal Nossa Senhora do Carmo, no bairro do Monte Santo. O horário ainda não foi informado pela família.

articles.title: Chuva em São José dos Campos: cidade em alerta após 91 mm em 48h | G1
articles.standfirst: Acumulado deixa o solo encharcado em áreas de risco. Segundo o Cemaden, tendência é de melhora nesta quarta-feira, mas previsão indica retorno da chuva mais forte no fim de semana.
articles.summary: Chuva em São José dos Campos atinge 91 mm e Cemaden alerta para risco de deslizamentos em áreas de encosta, com previsão de novas pancadas no fim de semana.
articles.body:
Dia nublado e fechado, com previsão de chuva em São José dos Campos — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

São José dos Campos registrou 91 milímetros de chuva nas últimas 48 horas, segundo dados das estações do Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden) registrados até às 7h desta quarta-feira (2). O acumulado deixa o município em alerta para o risco de deslizamentos de terra, principalmente em áreas onde o solo já está encharcado.

Apesar da redução no ritmo da chuva, o volume registrado nos últimos dias exige atenção. Com o solo encharcado, novas precipitações podem aumentar a possibilidade de movimentação de massa em áreas de encosta.

Segundo uma meteorologista do Cemaden, São José dos Campos teve os maiores acumulados da região, com registros entre 80 e 90 milímetros em alguns bairros. Há um alerta vigente para movimento de massa, mas a tendência é de melhora nesta quarta-feira (2).

A previsão indica que não deve haver chuva intensa em São José dos Campos nesta quarta. Caso chova, a expectativa é de precipitações fracas e ocasionais. No Litoral Norte, a chuva pode ser fraca e mais persistente ao longo do dia.

Apesar da melhora no tempo nesta quarta-feira, o Cemaden chama atenção para a possibilidade de retorno da chuva nos próximos dias. A previsão indica pancadas de chuva no sábado (5) e no domingo (6). Para segunda-feira (7), a expectativa é de chuva mais persistente em alguns pontos.

A condição preocupa porque o solo ainda estará encharcado após os acumulados registrados nos últimos dias. Por isso, o monitoramento das áreas de risco deve continuar durante o fim de semana.

Além de São José dos Campos, outras cidades da região também registraram volumes elevados nas últimas 48 horas:

A população que vive em áreas de risco deve ficar atenta a sinais de movimentação do solo, como rachaduras em paredes ou no terreno, árvores ou postes inclinados, surgimento de degraus no solo e estalos em estruturas.

Em caso de sinais de risco, a orientação é deixar o imóvel e procurar um local seguro. Também é importante acompanhar os alertas da Defesa Civil e evitar permanecer próximo a encostas durante períodos de chuva.

articles.title: Justiça suspende shows de Ana Castela e Gustavo Mioto em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão acatou pedido do Ministério Público que questionou o gasto de R$ 1,816 milhão para a realização da 40ª Festa da Banana.
articles.summary: Decisão acatou pedido do Ministério Público que questionou o investimento de R$ 1,816 milhão para a realização da 40ª Festa da Banana.
articles.body:
Ana Castela e Gustavo Mioto estão entre os artistas contratados para a 40ª Festa da Banana — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

A Justiça determinou a suspensão dos recursos destinados à contratação de artistas para a 40ª Festa da Banana, em Santa Bárbara do Tugúrio , no Campo das Vertentes. O evento acontece entre os dias 23 e 27 de setembro.

A decisão foi proferida pela 1ª Vara Cível da Comarca de Barbacena nesta terça-feira (1º). A medida atende uma ação civil pública ajuizada pelo Ministério Público de Minas Gerais (MPMG) , que questiona o gasto de R$ 1,816 milhão para a contratação dos artistas Ana Castela, Gustavo Mioto, Muriel Alves, Igor Ferrari, Yuri e Troy e Delino Marçal .

Segundo a Promotoria de Justiça de Defesa do Patrimônio Público de Barbacena, embora as contratações tenham sido feitas por meio de procedimentos de inexigibilidade de licitação, há indícios de que os valores não são compatíveis com a realidade financeira do município, que tem pouco mais de 4 mil habitantes.

A decisão destaca que a aplicação de recursos públicos deve observar os princípios da razoabilidade, proporcionalidade, eficiência e moralidade administrativa. De acordo com a magistrada, os elementos apresentados na ação indicam que as despesas para apresentações artísticas podem comprometer a realização dos serviços públicos essenciais.

Ainda de acordo com a Justiça, o município deverá se abster de realizar pagamentos, transferências, liquidações, emissões de empenho ou qualquer outra forma de repasse de recursos públicos destinados às apresentações artísticas contratadas para a festa. Em caso de descumprimento, foi fixada multa de R$ 200 mil por ato praticado em desacordo com a determinação judicial.

A decisão também impõe às empresas contratadas e aos representantes dos artistas a obrigação de não realizar, autorizar ou contribuir para a realização dos shows previstos. A liminar estabelece multa correspondente ao valor integral de cada contrato em caso de descumprimento e determina a devolução ao município de eventuais valores já recebidos antecipadamente.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Prefeitura de Santa Bárbara do Tugúrio para solicitar um posicionamento sobre a decisão da Justiça e aguarda retorno.

Valor supera arrecadação própria da cidade

Ao analisar a ação, a magistrada considerou os dados apresentados pelo MPMG, que revelam que o valor previsto apenas para a contratação dos artistas supera a arrecadação própria de Santa Bárbara do Tugúrio para 2026, estimada em cerca de R$ 930 mil .

A decisão também menciona o expressivo crescimento dos gastos municipais com festividades nos últimos anos e o remanejamento de recursos que deveriam ser destinados a áreas da administração pública para financiar eventos festivos.

O levantamento do Ministério Público apontou que as despesas passaram de aproximadamente R$ 1,6 milhão em 2024 para R$ 4,9 milhões em 2025. Na Festa da Banana, o crescimento ultrapassou 300% no período analisado.

articles.title: 7 de setembro: veja o que abre e fecha em Caruaru  | G1
articles.standfirst: Serviços e estabelecimentos terão mudanças no horário de funcionamento. Bancos estarão fechados.
articles.summary: Serviços e estabelecimentos terão mudanças no horário de funcionamento. Bancos estarão fechados.
articles.body:
Comércio de Caruaru — Foto: Prefeitura de Caruaru

Na próxima segunda-feira (7), é celebrado o feriado nacional do Dia da Independência do Brasil. Em Caruaru , no Agreste de Pernambuco, alguns estabelecimentos, serviços e centros de compra mudam o horário de funcionamento.

Confira o que abre e fecha em Caruaru no feriado:

Comércio de rua : As lojas que solicitarem autorização poderão praticar a jornada de trabalho normalmente.

Polo Caruaru : Funciona em horário normal, das 9h às 18h.

Shopping Difusora : Funciona em horário especial, com as lojas, praça de alimentação e quiosques abrindo às 11h e encerrando as atividades às 20h. O cinema irá funcionar conforme a programação própria.

Caruaru Shopping : O centro de compras do bairro Indianópolis irá funcionar em horário normal. Lojas, quiosques e serviços abrem de 10h e encerram as atividades de 22h. A praça de alimentação funciona das 11h às 22h. O supermercado abre de 8h e fecha às 22h. A academia irá funcionar em horário especial, das 8h às 18h. Os cinemas funcionam conforme o horário da sessão.

Bancos : As agências bancárias não estarão abertas para atendimento presencial ao público no feriado da Independência do Brasil, comemorado em 07 de setembro.

Vai trabalhar no feriado? Veja o que diz a lei

A data, considerada feriado nacional pela Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT), garante aos funcionários um dia de descanso.

Celebrado em 7 de setembro, o feriado marca a Independência do Brasil, proclamada em 1822, quando o país rompeu seus laços coloniais com Portugal.

Como a data cai em uma segunda-feira, quem folga aos fins de semana poderá ter três dias seguidos de descanso — de sábado a segunda-feira.

Enquanto alguns trabalhadores terão a oportunidade de aproveitar o feriado, outros seguirão trabalhando normalmente . A legislação permite o funcionamento de atividades em setores considerados essenciais.

⚠️ Mas atenção: quem for escalado para trabalhar no feriado tem direito a receber em dobro ou a uma folga compensatória. O g1 conversou com especialistas em direito trabalhista para explicar como funcionam as regras.

articles.title: Ohio Supreme Court denies Mackenzie Shirilla's latest appeal bid in double murder case
articles.summary: Mackenzie Shirilla suffered another setback after the Ohio Supreme Court refused to reconsider its decision not to review her latest appeal.
articles.body: Convicted double murderer Mackenzie Shirilla suffered another legal setback after the Ohio Supreme Court denied her attorneys' request to reconsider its decision not to hear her latest appeal. Shirilla, now 21, is serving two concurrent sentences of 15 years to life for killing her boyfriend, Dominic Russo, 20, and their friend, Davion Flanagan, 19, after prosecutors said she intentionally drove her Toyota Camry into a brick building in Strongsville, Ohio, in 2022. Chief Justice Sharon Kennedy denied Shirilla's motion for reconsideration after her attorneys asked the state's highest court to revisit its June 23 decision declining to review her case, according to court records. "It is ordered by the court that the motion for reconsideration in this case is denied," Kennedy wrote. MACKENZIE SHIRILLA'S TEXTS SURFACE AS 'HELL ON WHEELS' DRIVER'S APPEAL COLLIDES WITH NETFLIX'S 'THE CRASH' Tuesday's decision leaves intact a lower-court ruling that Shirilla's postconviction challenge was filed one day too late. Shirilla's attorneys have argued that the missed deadline resulted from confusion over the filing timeline, including a calendar mistake involving the 2024 leap year. The postconviction challenge sought to raise claims that Shirilla received ineffective assistance of counsel, including an argument that her trial lawyers failed to adequately investigate evidence that she suffered from Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome, or POTS. Her attorneys have argued that the condition could have caused Shirilla to lose consciousness before the crash and potentially explain why she failed to brake before impact. WATCH: MACKENZIE SHIRILLA’S FATHER CALLS HER ‘A DUMB 18-YEAR-OLD’ WHILE BERATING POLICE IN BODYCAM VIDEO The defense previously said the condition was only "cursorily referenced" at trial despite Shirilla and her family allegedly putting her attorneys on notice about it. The latest court decisions, however, have focused on whether Shirilla's postconviction petition was filed on time rather than the merits of those arguments. Under Ohio law, a postconviction petition must generally be filed within 365 days after the trial transcript is filed in the court of appeals. The court determined that the relevant transcript was filed Oct. 24, 2023, making the deadline Oct. 23, 2024. Shirilla filed her petition on Oct. 24, 2024, the 366th day. Shirilla argued that the clock should have started later, when juvenile bindover transcripts were filed, and also pointed to the 2024 leap year. The appellate court rejected both arguments, finding that the statute refers to the "trial transcript," not supplemental juvenile-hearing transcripts, and that the law provides 365 days, not a calendar year. IDAHO JUDGE GRANTS BRYAN KOHBERGER TWO HEARINGS NEXT YEAR AS ADMITTED KILLER SEEKS TO WITHDRAW GUILTY PLEA Her attorneys later asked the Ohio Supreme Court to review the case. The state's highest court declined to accept jurisdiction June 23 before Shirilla's legal team asked the justices to reconsider that decision. Shirilla's case has received renewed public attention following the release of Netflix's "The Crash." Shirilla was convicted in 2023 after a bench trial of four counts of murder, four counts of felonious assault and two counts of aggravated vehicular homicide. Prosecutors argued at trial that Shirilla intentionally drove into the building to end her toxic relationship with Russo and that Flanagan was an unintended victim who happened to be in the car. NEW HAMPSHIRE SUPREME COURT OVERTURNS ADAM MONTGOMERY'S MURDER CONVICTION IN DAUGHTER HARMONY'S DEATH Evidence presented in the case included surveillance video, vehicle "black box" data and evidence that Shirilla's car was traveling nearly 100 mph without braking before the crash, according to WOIO. Shirilla has maintained that the crash was not intentional. Her convictions were upheld on direct appeal in 2024. articles.title: 'He can remove Pakistan from world picture': Shinde on PM Modi's cropped SCO photo
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde criticised Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s Office for cropping Prime Minister Nare.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde criticised Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s Office for cropping Prime Minister Narendra Modi out of a photograph from the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, saying Pakistan should not attempt to “play such games” with India.“What Pakistan has done is extremely unfortunate. Pakistan has always attempted such things. However, I would say that while they may have removed Modi Ji’s photograph, if Modi Ji wants, he can remove Pakistan from the world picture,” Shinde said on Tuesday.His remarks came after Sharif’s office shared an edited version of the SCO family photograph that placed the Pakistani prime minister at the centre while cropping out several leaders. The original photograph, taken before a session of the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, showed the heads of member states standing together.“During Operation Sindoor, terrorists in Pahalgam committed a grave crime against our people and our sisters by wiping away their sindoor. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, our armed forces completely destroyed terrorist bases in Pakistan. They also destroyed 11 airbase camps and brought Pakistan to its knees,” he said.“The entire country is proud of the Indian armed forces and Prime Minister Modi’s leadership. Therefore, Pakistan should never attempt to play such games with our country,” Shinde added.He also said that editing Modi out of the photograph would not affect his standing in India or internationally.“I would also say that such an act of removing a photograph cannot erase Prime Minister Modi from the hearts of 140 crore Indians. In fact, Prime Minister Modi remains one of the most popular leaders in the world...”The 26th SCO summit, which marked the organisation’s 25th anniversary, focused on regional cooperation as well as security, economic and geopolitical challenges. The summit was held in the expanded “SCO Plus” format, bringing together leaders from member, partner and observer countries.Addressing the summit, PM Modi called for a united fight against terrorism and said there could be no “double standards” on the issue. articles.title: Nepal floods: Father borrows $13, walks for days to search for missing son
articles.summary: Poor, frustrated and angry, Talka Sada is losing hope after trekking across Nepal’s flood-hit areas in his search.
articles.body:
Kathmandu/Nuwakot, Nepal — Talka Sada’s eyes are exhausted, the wrinkles on his face deep with worry. His heels hurt after walking long miles across Nepal’s mountains. He’s hungry and angry, but as his mood shifts between hope and helplessness, his focus remains on his mission: a desperate search for his son.

Sada, who is in his 50s, is from Saptari, a district in Nepal’s Terai region — the plains that stretch across southern Nepal, south of the Shivalik Hills and north of the porous border with India.

People from this part of the Himalayan nation are known as Madhesis, a distinct ethnolinguistic population with a diverse regional, cultural and caste identity. Vinod, his only son — Sada also has three daughters — has been missing since the devastating flash floods of August 26 destroyed homes, schools, bridges, power plants and everything in their path in large parts of northern Nepal.

Sada last spoke to 19-year-old Vinod a day before the floods that grew from the Bhotekoshi river. Vinod had come to the Rasuwa district, the region worst affected by the floods, a month earlier to work as a labourer at a hydropower plant. He would mix cement and take on other odd jobs. Four other young men who worked with him — all between 17 and 19 years old — are also missing since the floods.

“I can’t tell you how much my wife is howling. I am in deep pain myself and I do not know what to do,” Sada says as he wipes his tears.

Dressed in a faded white shirt and black pants, the father wears an orange polythene bag as a raincoat. He carries a grey backpack on his shoulders. With him is his brother, Sada’s companion on a long and increasingly frustrating journey.

Sada shows a dirty handkerchief in his pocket with notes amounting to less than 2,000 Nepali rupees (about $13) crumpled in it. It’s money he borrowed to be able to crisscross Nepal’s flood-affected areas in search of his son.

“I borrowed money to come all the way from Saptari to here. I have to pay an interest of 20 rupees on every 100 rupees I have borrowed,” he says. The brothers used some of that money to take a bus from Saptari to the national capital, Kathmandu. That 292km (181-mile) journey takes nine hours because of Nepal’s hilly terrain.

In Kathmandu, Sada and his brother went from hospital to hospital to look for Vinod among survivors or in the list of those declared dead — many of the flood victims were flown into Kathmandu from the northern parts of Nepal.

Outside mortuaries, the photographs displayed are often difficult to recognise. Most bodies being retrieved are decomposed or dismembered. There was no sign of Vinod — nor his name or photo at the hospitals.

So, Sada started walking towards Nuwakot (nearly 60km away from Kathmandu), closer to the location of the hydropower plant where his son was believed to be working.

After a gruelling, hours-long walk through broken roads, they reached Trishuli, a town on the way whose market now lies covered with debris, mud and slush.

“Last night when we reached here, a lodge charged us 1,500 Nepali rupees to stay the night. They gave us only one small serving of rice that did not even satisfy our hunger,” says Sada. “Now if we have to stay here another night, all my remaining money will finish and I will be left with nothing to go back home.”

Sada and his brother say they just want access to mortuaries and army camps set up to help evacuate survivors and take bodies from the disaster zone, but claim that he has been turned away repeatedly.

To the brothers, the response they’ve received to their pleas for help is a product of deep-seated ethnic and caste divisions within Nepal. Madhesis — as the people of the Terai are known — have long accused the hills-based Nepali elite of discriminating against them.

Sada’s family is from the Musahar community, a particularly marginalised community that lives in the Terai and in the Indian states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

“We are poor. They think of us as Madheshis and Biharis. We cannot speak Nepali fluently — which is why they are just pushing us away and making us run from pillar to post,” Sada claims, as he sobs. “Even if it is a corpse, we have a right to see it. We have registered our names everywhere – police stations to military camps. But no one is helping us.”

Nepali authorities, overwhelmed by the scale of the crisis — more than 1,000 people have been killed, and thousands are still missing — insist they are trying their best to reach and help all survivors.

The brothers try dialling Vinod’s phone number for the umpteenth time, but get no response. “We can’t talk to him. We don’t hear his voice. So everyone is heartbroken back home,” says Sada. “My wife asked me to get our son back. So we are searching all hydropower plants, but where do I find him?”

One minute, Sada is hoping for a miracle. “My son is young. He is a porter. He is daily wager. So he is agile. He could have surely walked, ran somewhere,” he wonders.

The very next moment, though, the father’s voice rings with helplessness. “I have no hope,” he says. “If Vinod was alive, he surely would have called from somewhere, even if he went to drink water.”

Yet giving up isn’t an option — not yet, at least.

So, Sada and his brother prepare to continue their trek towards the power plant where Vinod worked. As they leave, the father issues a warning that rings with a sense of betrayal and anger.

“We will have to burn down the police station if no one answers or helps us,” he shouts.

articles.title: In 1940, Nazis seized a 3-inch painting from a Jewish collector in Vienna; 86 years later, Austria returned it to his heir in Minnesota
articles.summary: US News: An 1847 painting made by a not-so-popular artist wouldn't have much historical or monetary value for most. But to Jackie Sondell, whose three grandpar.
articles.body: An 1847 painting made by a not-so-popular artist wouldn't have much historical or monetary value for most. But to Jackie Sondell, whose three grandparents died in the Holocaust, it's a priceless family heirloom. The Austrian deputy consul general in the Twin Cities, from his posting in New York, lifted the top off a cardboard box and pulled out a tiny piece of art. The 1847 watercolour miniature, about 3 inches tall and 2 inches wide, showed a nobleman who was an officer in the Austrian Empire's army and was stolen from the house of Sondell's relative Eduard Epstein in Vienna, Austria, by the Nazis, as per a report by The Minnesota Star Tribune.It was painted by Albert Theer, an Austrian painter not much famed in history. For years, the miniature had been overlooked at the Museum of Military History in Vienna. Then, the Austrian diplomat handed over the painting to its rightful heir, Jackie Sondell, a retired real estate agent who lived in Wayzata. “I see it as a symbol of hope,” Sondell said.The Austrian government had tracked down the 77-year-old Sondell and her brother, Jeff Lieb, after officials learned the siblings were the heirs of Eduard Epstein. Epstein had been a successful Jewish merchant in the Viennese textile industry in the early 1900s and an enthusiastic art collector.But when the Nazis took control of Austria in 1938, Epstein's circumstances changed dramatically. His company was liquidated, and his valuables including jewellery, coin collections, and silver were requisitioned. When he tried to sell his art collection to fund an escape from the widening terror of the Nazis, he was caught and sent to prison for 10 months. He finally managed to flee to America in 1941 with his wife and daughter. Weakened by prison, he died two years later at 62. Epstein’s family never saw his art collection again, lost to the Nazis and to history.Return to the heirsIt was in 2013, when the miniature watercolour of the Austrian nobleman was identified in the Vienna military museum. It was submitted to an art restitution board, part of a broad effort across Austria in recent decades to return art stolen by the Nazis.Tracking down heirs to a painting stolen nearly a century ago can be difficult, explained the Austrian diplomat, Johannes Gassner. But last year a government representative tracked down Sondell and told her about the painting. Growing up, Sondell and her brother were close to their Aunt Helen and Uncle Ernest. Helen was the only daughter of Epstein and his wife, Margarete. Helen was not Sondell's blood relative, but had married into the family when she married Sondell's Uncle Ernest. Since Helen and Ernest didn’t have children, they treated Sondell and her brother like their own, spoiling them with summer trips to the Adirondacks or adventures in New York City. When Helen died in 2000, Sondell and her brother became heirs to her estate.Sondell called Dorotheum, one of the world’s oldest auction houses in Vienna, to learn about the miniature’s history. Researchers told her Epstein had been arrested when he tried to sell the art, which the Nazis seized on March 28, 1940.“Austria took a while to accept responsibility for its role in the crimes and atrocities committed by the Nazi regime,” Gassner said. “Of course you cannot undo what happened, and you cannot restore the lives of all those who were murdered. But nevertheless today’s restitution is an important gesture in the context of Austria’s efforts to live up to its historical responsibility. It’s never too late to accept responsibility.”As the diplomat travelled to Minnesota to return the painting, Sondell felt emotional. She thought about how her aunt Helen would have felt if she were alive. And how the Holocaust formed a part in her family's history, where she lost three grandparents to it: one in Dachau, two at the Sobibor extermination camp in Poland. “May their memories be a blessing,” Sondell said. Sondell’s mother escaped to London before making her way to the United States, but the Holocaust was never far from her mother’s mind.However belated it was for Austria to recognise its responsibility, Sondell appreciated it. She hopes the return of the painting highlights the individual Jewish lives brutally affected by the Holocaust. Six million Jews dead is a soul-numbing statistic, but Eduard Epstein’s story is a tragedy.“No matter what size the picture is, at least they are making the effort of returning it,” Sondell said. “You have to give somebody a second chance. If you stop and forgive, maybe the world will see things a different way. Maybe there is hope for peace in the world.”Interestingly, the miniature makes up just one piece of Epstein's large art collection. The whereabouts of the rest of his art still remain unknown with no full accounting of what was stolen.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1996, USGS released an 8-day Glen Canyon flood at 1,275 cubic metres per second to track sediment; 120 cross sections measured how the flood changed the Colorado River channel
articles.summary: US News: In 1996, USGS conducted a controlled flood to study sediment dynamics and restore natural habitat in the Colorado River. Discover the results and implications of this groundbreaking experiment.
articles.body: In March and April 1996, a planned high-flow experiment at Glen Canyon Dam released water at a rate of 1,275 cubic metres per second for eight days as scientists studied how the surge would affect the Colorado River downstream. The purpose was not to generate power or cope with an unexpected surge. It was to test whether an artificial flood could repair some of the damage the dam itself had caused to the river downstream, particularly the sandbars and beaches that had been quietly disappearing for more than thirty years.How Glen Canyon Dam changed the Colorado RiverGlen Canyon Dam was completed in 1963, and it changed the Colorado River almost overnight. Before the dam, spring snowmelt sent huge pulses of sediment-laden water crashing through Grand Canyon every year, scouring the channel and depositing fresh sand along the banks. Once the dam went up, that rhythm stopped. Lake Powell, the reservoir behind it, trapped nearly all the incoming sand, and the steadier, regulated releases from the dam no longer carried enough sediment to replenish the beaches. Over time, campsites and backwater habitats that native fish and plants depended on began to erode. Researchers had a theory that a short, powerful flood, timed correctly, might scoop sand off the riverbed and push it back onto the banks. Testing that theory meant watching the river extremely closely while the flood happened.Tracking sand at 120 points along the riverNearly a hundred geomorphologists and ecologists spread out along a 385-kilometre stretch of the Colorado, from Glen Canyon through Marble Canyon and into the Grand Canyon, to record what happened as the water rose. The US Geological Survey collected data at five streamflow gauging stations on the main river and four more on tributaries during the controlled flood, while river stage readings came from an additional 29 locations. To measure how much sand was actually shifting, crews documented changes in the channel bed by surveying a network of 120 fixed cross sections before and after the release. This level of detail let scientists compare, almost metre by metre, how the riverbed looked before the flood and how it looked once the water dropped back to normal levels. The findings from this and two later floods in 2004 and 2008 were eventually brought together to study how sediment behaves during these engineered surges, giving managers a much richer picture of the river's mechanics than a single event could ever provide.A flood that kept coming backThe immediate results were encouraging. Sandbars grew larger and reappeared in places where they had all but vanished, and researchers found no lasting harm to plant or animal communities living along the banks. The 1996 high-flow experiment was designed to test whether a controlled release could redistribute sediment and rebuild sandbars downstream of Glen Canyon Dam. Subsequent monitoring found that the flood did increase sandbar size in parts of the Grand Canyon, although the gains were not permanent. The benefits were temporary. Monitoring of the high-flow experiments showed that sandbars can erode again under subsequent river conditions because the dam continues to restrict the amount of sediment reaching the Grand Canyon. That lesson helped shift management toward a more condition-based approach, in which high-flow experiments are considered when enough sediment has accumulated downstream and hydrologic conditions are suitable, rather than simply being scheduled at regular intervals.After the 1996 experiment, high-flow experiments were conducted again in 2004 and 2008, followed by further releases under a longer-term protocol beginning in 2012. Later experiments took place in 2013, 2014, 2016, 2018 and 2023. What began as a one week test of a bold hypothesis has turned into an ongoing, decades long relationship between engineers and a river they permanently altered but never stopped trying to understand. The controlled floods have given scientists more data on how sediment, sandbars and river habitats respond to large releases below Glen Canyon Dam, helping managers refine how and when future experiments should be conducted.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Bus crash in Egypt’s South Sinai kills at least 21
articles.summary: Bus crashes on Dahab-Nuweiba road on the eastern coast of the Sinai Peninsula, an area popular with tourists.
articles.body:
A bus crash in Egypt’s South Sinai governorate has killed at least 21 people and injured more than 20 others, the Ministry of Health and Population said.

The incident happened on Wednesday morning on the road from Dahab to Nuweiba on the eastern coast of the Sinai Peninsula, an area with resorts along the Red Sea popular with tourists.

A number of Jordanians were on the bus and initial information indicated several were killed and ⁠injured, Jordan’s foreign ministry ⁠said.

Jordan’s state media reported that 10 of the victims in the crash were Jordanian nationals, adding that the bus was carrying 43 people in total, including 22 Jordanians.

Egypt’s Health Ministry spokesman Hossam Abdel Ghaffar said 20 ambulances were dispatched to the scene to evacuate and treat the wounded.

Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar ordered medical facilities to raise their level of preparedness and provide the injured with necessary medical care, medicines and supplies.

Deadly road accidents are common in Egypt. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country , according to Egypt’s state statistics agency.

Last month, 18 people ⁠were killed ⁠and 30 ⁠injured in a road accident in the northeastern governorate of Ismailia.

articles.title: In 2015, Florida scientists poured 5 gallons of red dye into Silver River to study how water moved as its clear waters were turning algae-green; they found it took roughly 11.5 hours to travel 5.1 miles.
articles.summary: US News: In 2015, a groundbreaking study using fluorescent dye in Florida's Silver River provided insights into water movement and ecological shifts. The research revealed that water traveled 5.1 miles in approximately 11.5 hours, shedding light on the relationship between flow dynamics and algal growth.
articles.body: In 2015, researchers used a fluorescent dye to trace the movement of water through the Silver River, one of Florida’s major spring-fed waterways. The experiment was designed to measure how quickly water travelled through the river, how it mixed along the way and how long it remained in different sections.According to the University of Florida’s Center for Wetlands and Stream Ecosystem Research, the 2015 dye-tracing experiment was part of a broader research effort examining changes in Florida’s spring ecosystems. These included a shift from clear-water conditions dominated by submerged aquatic vegetation towards greater algal growth. Researchers were investigating how changes in river hydraulics and nutrient movement might be related to these ecological changes.A dye turns invisible movement into a measurable signalOn March 8, 2015, researchers from the University of Florida’s Watershed Ecology Lab released five gallons of Rhodamine ET, a red fluorescent dye, at the Main Spring vent in the Silver River. They tracked the dye downstream using nine monitoring stations, including three in-stream fluorometers and six automated samplers. More than 20 student volunteers also collected 318 additional samples overnight. These measurements allowed researchers to calculate the river’s velocity and residence time, referring to how long water remained within the monitored system and its different sections.Fluorescent dye tracing is commonly used to study the movement and mixing of water because the tracer can be detected at successive points along a river. In the Silver River, the method allowed researchers to follow the same water signal downstream rather than relying only on measurements taken at individual locations. The 2015 results showed that the dye travelled the roughly 5.1-mile monitored reach in about 11.5 hours, according to the project’s reported results. That works out to an average travel rate of about 0.44 miles per hour, although the dye did not move at the same rate throughout the river.What the tracer revealed about the riverResearchers later compared the 2015 results with those from another Silver River tracer experiment carried out in 2009. A University of Florida Water Institute study found that the river’s hydraulic behaviour changed under different discharge conditions. At higher discharge, the mean residence time of the spring run decreased, while transient storage increased. In practical terms, this means that changes in river flow can affect both how quickly water travels downstream and how much water temporarily exchanges with slower-moving areas along the channel. Such changes can, in turn, influence how nutrients and other substances move through the river.The researchers were also examining whether these hydraulic conditions were related to differences in algal biomass. Initial findings from the University of Florida showed a negative correlation between water velocity and algal cover in benthic and periphytic habitats. The tracer experiments therefore provided a way to examine the physical conditions alongside the biological observations. Where water moves faster, organisms experience different flow conditions than in areas where water remains longer. These differences can affect the transport and retention of nutrients and other substances, helping researchers examine how changes in river flow may be associated with changes in the river’s biological communities.Following the river to understand its changing ecologyThe Silver River experiment formed part of a larger three-year interdisciplinary research project funded by the St Johns River Water Management District. Ten University of Florida researchers from four departments contributed to the programme, which examined the causes of ecological change in Florida’s springs and possible responses. The tracer experiment focused on how water moved through the Silver River, providing measurements that helped researchers understand the physical conditions within the spring system.The tracer data were also used to calibrate and validate a model of water movement and dye transport through the river. By tracking the tracer from the spring vent downstream, researchers were able to measure how quickly it travelled through different sections of the river and compare those observations with the model's predictions. This provided a more detailed picture of water movement through the system and helped place the biological changes observed in the river within their underlying hydrological conditions.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Archaeologists uncover a residential complex and possible ancient wine press near the Temple of Sekhmet at Egypt’s Memphis
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Archaeologists working at the ancient Egyptian city of Memphis have uncovered a residential complex and a collection of artefacts near the Temple of S.
articles.body: Archaeologists working at the ancient Egyptian city of Memphis have uncovered a residential complex and a collection of artefacts near the Temple of Sekhmet in Mit Rahina, Giza. An Egyptian-Chinese archaeological mission discovered the site during excavations on August 30, according to Egypt’s State Information Service. Among the findings is a limestone structure that researchers believe may have been used as a wine press, while grape seeds recovered from the area further support this identification. The team also found stone blocks with inscriptions, fragments of statues, and other architectural remains. The discoveries offer a glimpse into activity around one of Memphis’s temple areas and add new evidence to the archaeological picture of the ancient city.What did the Egyptian-Chinese team discover at ancient MemphisAn Egyptian-Chinese archaeological mission has uncovered the remains of a residential complex near the Temple of Sekhmet at Mit Rahina in Giza. Archaeologists identified mud-brick remains that formed part of the complex, along with artefacts and architectural remains. The mission recovered stone blocks carrying inscriptions and statue fragments. These findings provide evidence of activity around the temple. Mit Rahina was the site of Memphis, a major centre of Egyptian civilisation, and the remains add another layer to Memphis’s archaeological record.Grape seeds offer clues to a possible ancient wine pressOne notable discovery is a limestone structure that archaeologists believe may have been used as a wine press. Grape seeds found in the area provide further evidence for this possibility. The structure adds to the growing picture of activity around the temple and suggests that the site was used for more than religious purposes. It was found alongside the remains of the residential complex and other artefacts uncovered during the excavation. For archaeologists, the structure offers another clue to how this part of ancient Memphis was used. Further examination of the limestone installation and the material found around it could help establish its exact purpose and reveal more about the activities that once took place at Mit Rahina.What do the inscriptions and statue fragments reveal about Mit RahinaThe excavation has uncovered several findings that shed light on the architectural and artistic character of the site. Among them, there are stone blocks bearing inscriptions and fragments of statues, found alongside the remains of the residential complex and the limestone structure. Together, these discoveries offer clues about the people, buildings, and activities that once shaped this part of Mit Rahina. The inscribed blocks may provide valuable information about structures or individuals linked to the site, while the statue fragments offer a glimpse into its artistic and religious setting. Rather than being isolated objects, the findings form part of a wider archaeological context.How did life around the Temple of Sekhmet change over timeThe discoveries are helping archaeologists examine how different parts of ancient Memphis were used around the Temple of Sekhmet. The remains point to a landscape where residential spaces, structures linked to daily activities, and religious architecture existed within the same wider setting. The mud-brick complex provides evidence of habitation, while the limestone installation and grape seeds offer clues about activities that took place at the site. Inscribed stone blocks and statue fragments add another layer by connecting the physical remains with the artistic and cultural traditions of Memphis.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: Tech News News: The US Treasury Department has unveiled new guidance that could make it easier for millions of American families to grow their Trump Accounts through .
articles.body: The US Treasury Department has unveiled new guidance that could make it easier for millions of American families to grow their Trump Accounts through workplace payroll contributions. The announcement comes months after Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell and his wife Susan Dell pledged $6.25 billion to Trump Accounts through the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation to support the child savings initiative, one of the largest commitments made to the programme. Announcing the new update, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said: “Trump Accounts are giving American families a new way to build wealth from day one”.Trump Accounts get new payroll contribution rulesThe new Treasury guidance allows employers to make tax-free contributions of up to $2,500 a year for employees' dependent children and lets workers contribute pre-tax money directly from their paychecks into their children's Trump Accounts. As announced by the Treasury Department and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), the new framework allows:Employers to contribute up to $2,500 tax-free each year to an employee's dependent child's Trump Account.Employees to make pre-tax payroll contributions to their children's Trump Accounts through employer cafeteria plans.Employer contributions to be excluded from an employee's taxable income, subject to the programme's rules.“Today, Treasury is publishing guidance that will help families grow Trump Accounts by allowing employers to contribute up to $2,500 tax-free each year for employees' dependents and giving employees the option to contribute pre-tax dollars directly to those accounts,” Bessent said.Michael Dell's $6.25 billion pledgeThe latest rules follow the $6.25 billion commitment announced by Michael Dell and Susan Dell in December 2025. The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation said it would use the funds to help launch the child savings programme, then known as Trump Accounts and later renamed Invest America Accounts. The donation is intended to provide $250 to the accounts of 25 million American children when the programme begins, making it the foundation's largest-ever philanthropic commitment.The Treasury's latest guidance is expected to make it easier for employers to participate in the programme that the Dell Foundation has backed financially.More than 50 companies have already signed upAccording to the Treasury Department, more than 50 companies have already committed to making Trump Account contributions for employees' children. The department said this means even children who do not qualify for the government's $1,000 Treasury seed contribution can still receive tax-free employer contributions into their accounts.The Treasury also said the programme gives businesses "a new, low-cost, tax-preferred benefit" that can help attract and retain workers while helping families save for the future.What employers must doTo establish a Trump Account employer contribution program, the employer must:Maintain a separate written plan document;Follow certification procedures that permit employers to rely on employees’ self-certification of the Trump Account beneficiary’s age and dependent status, but require validation that the account into which the contribution will be made is a Trump Account;Provide notices to employees;Provide annual statements to employees; andProvide reporting to the Trump Account trustee.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Bespoke guitar raffle to raise money for Rothbury Estate
articles.summary: Proceeds of the raffle will help fund conservation groups' bid to buy the Northumberland estate.
articles.body:
A "one of a kind" guitar is being raffled to help raise funds for conservation groups attempting to buy the Rothbury Estate in Northumberland.

Curvy Sounds, in Heaton have customised a Tokai, Les Paul guitar which has already attracted interest from musicians from across the North East.

Jess Mills, co-owner of the guitar shop said: "Rothbury is a special place for us, it's such an important cause to restore that area and this is just our little way of helping."

Currently Wildlife Trusts and Northumberland Wildlife Trust have raised £26.2m of a £30m target to purchase the 3,800 hectare (15-sq-m) site in Northumberland, with plans to boost wildlife, restore bogs and promote nature-friendly farming.

Guitar maker Andrew Mills said he began to modify the guitar three years ago.

It was originally plain black but has since been decorated with more than 100 pieces of mother of pearl, resin and mirror plate.

"It's inspired by a make called Zemaitis who made guitars for Ronnie Wood, Donovan and George Harrison, I loved their pearl tops but this is one of a kind.

"It's taken the best part of three months to finish it off and you'd probably struggle to make another one, actually I'd even struggle to make it again," Andrew added.

He said £3,000 has been raised so far through raffle sales which will be donated to the Wildlife Trusts to buy the Rothbury Estate.

Conservation groups attempting to buy the entirety of the estate have just over a month to secure £3.8m.

North East musicians including Duncan Lloyd from Maximo Park, jazz singer Faye MacCalman, Nev Clay and luthier Terry Doherty have all entered the raffle.

Local artists Claire Webster-Saaremets and Harriet Menter have also been raising funds through selling artwork and photography.

Jess Mills said she had been "overwhelmed by the support" from the local community.

"We wanted to help and the community have backed us, we are yet to have a date for when the raffle will take place but we're hoping it will be later this month," she added.
